messages:
Maya R: Heads-up — noticed a correctness regression when running activation-quantized FP8 matmul with KV cache enabled on long chat traces (~>2048). Model diverges from FP16 baseline after ~30 tokens, deterministic repro.
Jun Park: Can you share a minimal repro and the exact config you ran? Is this on dedicated infra or hosted? Any recent kernel selector changes?
Maya R: Repro is on dedicated GPU pool (p4d). No recent config flips on our side. Quick config:
```json
{
  \"model\": \"redwood-v1-mini-mix\",
  \"precision\": \"mixed\",
  \"activation_quant\": \"fp8\",
  \"kv_cache\": true,
  \"batching\": { \"max_batch\": 8, \"dynamic_coalesce\": true }
}
```
Repro script (short):
```bash
python tests/repro_activation_fp8.py --seq 4096 --prompt-file smoke.txt
```
Jun Park: Got it. Any profiling or kernel-selection logs? If the selector is choosing the fp8 matmul kernel unexpectedly for certain sequence+batch shapes that could explain it.
Maya R: Pasted key counters from profiler run (nvtx + runtime counters):
```
matmul_fp8_opt: 74.1% time
matmul_bf16_fallback: 5.3% time
kernel_selector_votes: { fp8: 412, bf16: 113 }
kv_cache_reuse_rate: 0.87
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.13
scale_applied: 0.993 (calib expected 1.0)
attention_recompute_count: 0
```
Eli Torres: That scale_applied stuck at 0.993 is suspicious. If calibration is run on cold runs (no KV) and we reuse cached KV blocks without recomputing per-block scale, the quantization distribution could shift. In other words, KV reuse + dynamic batching may change activation histograms.
Jun Park: Good point. Also note dynamic_coalesce can change the sequence-length distribution the selector sees — maybe the selector's heuristic for preferring fp8 assumes the scale is stable across concatenated KV chunks.
Maya R: I tried forcing kernel selection to bf16 for all matmuls and correctness returns (diff==0 against FP16 baseline) but perf drops ~18%.
Anya L: Can you attach a small diff showing the failing tokens or a seed so we can reproduce locally? Also assign owners.
Maya R: Repro + seed attached in thread. Created minimal failing assert in tests/ci/activation_kv_repro.py.
perf-bot: perf job #4521 queued (eng-runtime / activation-quant / repro). ETA 12m.
Jun Park: Plan — I'll add per-request kernel-selection logging (kernel id + applied scale + kv_block_index) and a short guard that recomputes scale on KV cache hits for blocks older than one quantization-window. If that fixes correctness we can try a cheaper heuristic (invalidate scale when batch coalescing detected).
Eli Torres: Also add an eval that compares token logits across seq lengths (cold vs with KV hits). I suspect the tail tokens get scaled-off causing softmax shifts.
Maya R: Quick local patch I tested that fixes correctness (pseudocode):
```python
# in kernel_selector.py
if kv_cache.enabled and kv_cache.hit(block_idx):
    if block_age(block_idx) > SCALE_TOLERANCE:
        recompute_scale = True
else:
    recompute_scale = False

if recompute_scale:
    scale = recompute_activation_scale(block_data)
else:
    scale = cached_scale

choose_kernel_based_on(scale, activation_stats)
```
Jun Park: LGTM as an experiment. If perf drop is ~18%, maybe we only recompute for final-n layers or for attention blocks with high KL shift.
Anya L: Created issue #789: \"activation-quant: scale mismatch when reusing KV cache causes FP8 matmul correctness regression\" — assigned Jun + Eli. Added link to repro and perf job.
Maya R: Adding a couple more notes: (1) observed that the selector sometimes flips between fp8 and bf16 mid-request when batcher coalesces requests with different seq lengths — leads to mixed outputs, (2) serialization of scale metadata in KV was missing atomic ordering in one codepath.
Jun Park: I'll look into the atomic ordering bug, that could explain stale scale reads. Updating reproduction and will push a diagnostic build to the dedicated pool.
perf-bot: perf job #4521 finished — baseline vs diagnostic: latency +2%, correctness diff -> 0 for repro cases where recompute_scale=True.
Maya R: Thanks — marking this as high-priority. I'll keep the thread updated with experiments on cheaper heuristics (per-layer age threshold, KL-trigger).
